 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Seeking to halt a six-game winless run capped by a 1-0 defeat to the Edmonton Oilers, the Toronto Maple Leafs face the Chicago Blackhawks on Tuesday night. Toronto was outscored 23-9 during that difficult homestand, and the team needs to find a way to put the puck in the net against a Chicago defense that allows 4.10 goals per game. This matchup at the United Center marks the first time these two Original Six clubs have squared off this season, and both teams are desperate for a win to climb the standings.
 Goaltender Anthony Stolarz made 22 saves in the loss to the Oilers, but the Maple Leafs managed only 19 shots on goal. An apparent goal by John Tavares was taken away after a video review showed he deflected a William Nylander shot with a high stick, according to the BIG 1050 . The team's scoring leader, Auston Matthews, recorded just two shots in that game and has only one goal and five points over the six-game stretch.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Weight of Recent Results
 John Tavares spoke about the difficulty of dealing with a losing streak and the pressure to produce points. He noted that while players try not to focus too much on the score, the results are what matter most in the standings. Tavares admitted that the team feels the weight of the losses and knows they must work through the tough times to become better.
 Coach Jim Hiller expressed frustration that the team did not get the results they deserved despite playing hard. He said the players gave their all but still ended up on the wrong side of the scoreboard. Hiller emphasized that the team deserves better than the six-game skid and that they must move forward to the next challenge. The loss to the Oilers was the second shutout of the season for Toronto, adding to the frustration of a team that prides itself on scoring.
 The statistics show a clear need for improvement across the board for the Maple Leafs. They rank 15th in the league in goals scored per game with 3.14 and 20th in shots allowed with 29. The team has accumulated 18 points so far this season, placing them 13th in the Eastern Conference. This performance is far below the expectations for a franchise with such high offensive talent, and the upcoming game against Chicago offers a chance to reset.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Blackhawks Struggle to Protect Leads
 Also struggling, the Chicago Blackhawks sit next-to-last in the NHL, surrendering 4.10 goals per game. They stopped a six-game winless streak with an overtime victory against the Buffalo Sabres on Thursday, but they lost that chance to win consecutive games on Saturday against the Winnipeg Jets. The Jets scored four unanswered goals to force overtime and then won in the shootout on a goal by Kyle Connor. This pattern of blowing leads has been a major issue for Chicago this season.
 Blackhawks coach Jeff Blashill acknowledged that his team got on their heels too much during the game against Winnipeg. He praised the team for checking well in the first half and dictating the play, but he noted that they eventually sat back and let the opponent take control. Blashill said the team ended plays well in the offensive and neutral zones early on, but they failed to maintain that intensity for the full game. This lack of consistency has kept the Blackhawks near the bottom of the Western Conference.
 Chicago has a record of 5-13-2 this season and sits 15th in the Western Conference with 12 points. They rank 31st in the league in goals scored with 2.3 per game and 31st in shots with 23 per game. The team also struggles on special teams, ranking 30th in power play percentage at 14.29% and 15th in penalty kill percentage at 78.13%. These numbers highlight the defensive and offensive issues that both teams face heading into Tuesday night.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Key Players and Recent Performances
 Auston Matthews leads the Maple Leafs with 29 points, including 12 goals and 17 assists. He ranks seventh in the NHL in goals and eighth in points this season. William Nylander has added 22 points with 11 goals and 11 assists, while Jack Roslovic has contributed 20 points in 21 games. Despite these individual numbers, the team as a whole has failed to convert that talent into wins during the recent homestand. The loss of momentum is a significant concern for the coaching staff.
 For the Blackhawks, Connor Bedard has been a bright spot, recording six goals and 11 assists to help lead the offense. Roman Kantserov leads all NHL rookies with nine goals and has 12 points total. Teuvo Teravainen has been effective against Toronto in the past, and he registered two assists in the last game against the Winnipeg Jets. The team is hoping that these offensive leaders can spark a turnaround against the Maple Leafs, who have struggled to stop the puck in recent weeks.
 Goaltending has also been a challenge for both sides. Spencer Knight has a record of 5-10-1 for Chicago with a 3.60 goals-against average and an .882 save percentage. On the Toronto side, Sergei Bobrovsky has a record of 3-8-2 with 334 saves but has allowed 45 goals in 13 games. The goaltenders will need to make key saves if their teams hope to break their respective losing streaks and secure a win on Tuesday night.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Injury Updates and Roster Availability
 Several key players are dealing with injuries that could impact the lineup for Tuesday's game. Tyler Bertuzzi missed practice on Monday after leaving the game against Winnipeg with an upper-body injury, but coach Jeff Blashill expects him to play against Toronto. The Blackhawks also have Bowen Byram out with an upper-body injury and Ryan Ellis out for the season with a back injury. These absences affect the depth and physicality of the Chicago roster.
 The Maple Leafs are also dealing with a significant list of injuries that has weakened their lineup. Colton Sissons and Kirill Marchenko are all out with lower-body issues, while Cade Webber and Marshall Rifai are out with elbow and lower-body injuries respectively. Miles Wood is out with an undisclosed injury, and Max Domi is out with a back issue. The team has lost key contributors to the roster, which makes the task of scoring goals even more difficult.
 Despite the injury concerns, both teams are expected to field competitive lines for the matchup. The absence of players like Bertuzzi and Rielly will force coaches to adjust their strategies and rely on younger or less experienced players to step up. The depth chart will be tested as the game progresses, and the ability to adapt to these missing pieces could be the deciding factor in the outcome of the game.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Historical Context of the Matchup
 Patrick Kane has had success against Toronto in his career, totaling 21 points in 10 games at the United Center. In his last appearance against the Maple Leafs in February 2023, Kane collected four points in a single game. Teuvo Teravainen has also found success against Toronto at home, scoring goals in back-to-back games against them at the United Center. These historical performances suggest that the Blackhawks have the personnel to challenge the Maple Leafs on their home ice.
 Marking the initial clash of two this season, this upcoming game precedes a second meeting set for January 14, 2027, in Toronto. This matchup is a critical test for both franchises as they look to improve their standings. The winner will gain valuable points in the conference race, while the loser will face even more pressure to turn their season around. The history between these two Original Six clubs adds an extra layer of intensity to the game.
 Special Teams and Tactical Adjustments
 Special teams will play a crucial role in the outcome of the game, as both teams have struggled to capitalize on their opportunities. The Maple Leafs rank sixth in the league with a 26.67% power play percentage, which is one of their strongest assets. However, they have failed to convert this advantage into wins during their recent losing streak. The Blackhawks, on the other hand, rank 30th in power play percentage at 14.29%, which is a major weakness they must address.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Chicago forward Anton Frondell emphasized the need for players to stay strong on the puck and win battles in the corners. He stated that players must do off-ice work to maintain balance and use their sticks in different ways to gain an advantage. Frondell also noted that stick-on-puck and body contact are effective ways to win possession and create scoring chances. These tactical adjustments are essential for the Blackhawks to improve their performance against a skilled Maple Leafs team.
 The penalty kill is another area where both teams need to improve. The Maple Leafs rank seventh in the league with an 85.71% penalty kill percentage, while the Blackhawks rank 15th at 78.13%. The ability to kill penalties will be vital for Chicago, as they have struggled to prevent goals when shorthanded. The Maple Leafs will look to exploit this weakness on the power play, while the Blackhawks will need to tighten up their defensive structure to avoid giving up easy goals.
 The Road Ahead for Both Teams
 The loss to the Winnipeg Jets on Saturday was a missed opportunity for the Blackhawks to build momentum after their win against Buffalo. The team allowed a four-goal lead to slip away, which is a recurring theme in their season. Coach Blashill and the players know that they cannot afford to make the same mistakes again against the Maple Leafs. The game on Tuesday night is a chance to prove that they can close out games and secure a win at home.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement For the Maple Leafs, the focus is on breaking the losing streak and getting back on track. The team has the talent to score goals, but they have been unable to do so consistently in recent weeks. Coach Jim Hiller and the players must find a way to generate more offense and convert their chances into goals. The game against the Blackhawks provides a favorable matchup on paper, but the team must execute their game plan to avoid another disappointing result.
 Both teams are facing a critical juncture in their season, and the outcome of this game could have significant implications for their playoff hopes. The Maple Leafs need to rediscover their scoring touch, while the Blackhawks need to find a way to protect leads and win games at home. The matchup on Tuesday night will be a key test for both franchises as they look to turn their seasons around and climb the standings.
